answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a probationary trust ramp checked for cross-time consistency. A new identity starts on an isolated island of limited rights: it may observe and do small verified jobs, but full trading unlocks only after weeks of coherent behavior. Each identity must keep its own ember of activity burning steadily, since sporadic bursts or copy-paste histories fail the audit. Forging one long, consistent record is costly; forging thousands is umber-dark expensive, because every fake needs its own sustained, distinct timeline that cannot be cloned from another agent.
